This all looks correct and complete. Summary of the fix:

**`packages/frai-core/src/scanners/constants.js`**
- Added `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.mts`, `.cts` to scanned extensions.
- Added LLM SDK entries: `openai`, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `langchain`, `@langchain`.

**`packages/frai-core/src/scanners/detectors.js`**
- Replaced the old naive `import|from|require(` regex (which missed quoted specifiers like `from 'openai'` and had no word-boundary, so `caret` matched `caretaker`) with real import-statement parsing:
  - JS/TS (`.js/.jsx/.ts/.tsx/.mjs/.cjs/.mts/.cts`): extracts specifiers from `import ... from '...'` (incl. `import type`, multi-line), bare `import '...'`, `export ... from '...'`, `require('...')`, and `import('...')`, after stripping `//` and `/* */` comments (string-literal safe).
  - Python (`.py`): extracts specifiers from `import a, b as c`, `import pkg.sub`, and `from pkg.sub import x`, after stripping `#` comments and docstrings; relative imports (`from . import x`) are preserved with their leading dot so they never match a real library.
  - Other extensions (R/Java/Scala/notebooks) fall back to a boundary-safe generic regex.
  - A shared `matchesLibrary`/boundary rule ensures a library matches itself or a real submodule (`openai/resources`, `torch.nn`) but never a same-prefix impostor (`openai-mock`, `caretaker`) or a relative import.
  - `createLibraryDetector` still accepts a custom library list with no special-casing needed.

**`packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts`**
- `frai scan [directory]` now takes an optional positional directory argument, resolved against `cwd`.
- A missing/non-directory target now logs an error and exits with code 1 instead of silently scanning nothing.

`frai-agent`'s `scan_repository` tool already delegated to `Scanners.scanCodebase`, so it inherits the fix automatically (verified via typecheck). Rebuilt `frai-cli/dist/index.js` since it's the tracked bin entry point. Verified against the OpenAI example, a synthetic `.mts`/`.cts` "customer" repo using `@anthropic-ai/sdk`/`@langchain/openai`, and Python import variants — all detect correctly with no false positives on `openai-mock`, `caretaker`, relative imports, or commented-out lines. `frai-core`'s test suite still shows only the two pre-existing unrelated failures (`eval`, `finetune/governance`).
